review_kind: fresh independent Phase 0 adversarial review of v4

reviewer.lens: ADR conformance, finite local grammar, direct links, trusted seams, and non-authorizing boundary

scope_checked: scalar, signature, ID, recursive-shape, sort, uniqueness, and self-digest grammars
P(CES)/P(BVP)/P(CAS), profiles, chronology, equality, and inequality rules
injected signer/clock/revocation boundary and output/effect semantics
local decidability without a resolver or caller-selected schema

findings.invariant: The packet must define one executable, exact supplied-byte set that can prove the ADR PIS and P(CES)==P(BVP)==P(CAS) requirements.
findings.evidence: The six listed positions are ScopeIntent, CES, PEA, BVP, CAS, and one selected admission, although the request and every time rule say seven. PIS is absent. BVP contains only planned_capture_set_sha256, not the exact PlannedCaptureSet/PCE bytes needed to compute P(BVP); plan_sha256 is likewise only a token. CAS has entries, so the claimed local three-way projection comparison has no BVP operand.
adr_citations: ADR-0125 decision-log.md:8430-8445 defines the signed PIS and requires CES/PCE projections byte-identical to its named entry.
ADR-0125 decision-log.md:8663-8680 defines the exact PlannedCaptureSet/PCE operand and requires byte-for-byte P(CES)==P(BVP), including PIS projections, order, and cardinality.
ADR-0125 decision-log.md:8681-8691 extends that equality to CAS.
findings.worked_counterexample: A six-byte input can contain a canonical, correctly signed BVP whose planned_capture_set_sha256 equals CAS but whose unseen PlannedCaptureSet has different PCE entries. All v4 H and direct-digest checks can pass because no BVP PCE bytes were supplied, yet P(CES)!=P(BVP). Conversely, adding PIS and PlannedCaptureSet bytes violates the stated exact-seven/cardinality rule.
findings.consequence: The matrix either rejects a required operand or accepts an unprovable predecessor substitution; P3V4-02 and P3V4-07 cannot be implemented as claimed.
findings.required_correction: Choose and name a coherent supplied-byte set, with its exact cardinality and position map, and include every local operand needed for each claimed equality. Otherwise delete the P(BVP)/PIS verification claim and do not label the result ADR verification.

findings.invariant: A code-pinned exact schema must determine every accepted application scalar and the digest/signature bytes without a hidden schema.
findings.evidence: The envelope tables list bare application keys (for example study_id, phase, purpose, consumer_document_sha256, action_id, logical_execution_id, and run_id) rather than scalar/shape rules. The local-self sentence first says to omit only self, then gives a different signed-envelope rule. B64 is called canonical but has no alphabet, padding, decoded-byte, or keyring argument contract. The only existing keyring interface accepts an unspecified signature argument (trust.py:198-214), so the table cannot determine whether distinct encoded strings or decoded bytes reach Ed25519 verification.
adr_citations: ADR-0125 decision-log.md:8355-8362 requires closed default-deny canonical JSON and says both digest and Ed25519 preimage omit the named self digest and signature.
ADR-0125 decision-log.md:8539-8565 and 8620-8674 give the exact typed ActionIntent and CES/PEA/BVP application shapes, not merely key names.
findings.worked_counterexample: A validly signed CES with a numeric consumer_document_sha256 or an invalid phase representation is not refused by any v4 table entry: it is a bare key. Two implementations can also select different B64 padding/alphabet/decoding rules yet both satisfy the prose canonical base64, producing incompatible signature verification for identical supplied bytes.
findings.consequence: The promised private constants cannot independently implement P3V4-03/P3V4-05. Acceptance becomes an implementation-specific or hidden schema decision, contrary to the checkpoint's finite code-pinned grammar approach.
findings.required_correction: Replace every bare application key with an exact scalar, closed union, array, or nested-shape rule; state one unambiguous signed-object digest/preimage rule; and define B64's RFC variant, padding, decoding, and the exact value passed to ReleaseKeyring.verify.

findings.invariant: A value called an ADR-0125 verified envelope must verify its issuance basis and the required direct basis refs; a syntax-only H token is not that proof.
findings.evidence: v4 explicitly classifies issuance_basis_sha256 as unresolved and forbids fetching/parsing/validating its target. It therefore never supplies or verifies IssuanceBasis.v1, its signature, kind, sorted refs, phase-specific tuple, or key-use mapping. Revocation is separately delegated, but no analogous trusted basis verifier/injected basis bytes exists.
adr_citations: ADR-0125 decision-log.md:8359-8388 requires a verifier to check basis and every linked digest, and defines IssuanceBasis.v1 plus its closed refs and required signer/key-use mapping.
ADR-0125 decision-log.md:8613-8639 requires PEA's exact phase/tag basis facts; decision-log.md:8663-8666 requires the BVP basis and exact PCE-bearing plan.
findings.worked_counterexample: A correctly signed PEA with the right visible issuer_role/key_usage can name an arbitrary syntactically valid issuance_basis_sha256 rather than a basis naming its PIS, CES, intent, and phase authority. The v4 parser returns a VerifiedEnvelopes value because no supplied or trusted basis check can reject it.
findings.consequence: Wrong-predecessor and wrong-authority substitutions that ADR-0125 requires to refuse are accepted as verified. Making the output non-authorizing limits immediate effects but does not make the claimed verification or Packet 3 predecessor-refusal criterion true.
findings.required_correction: Either add exact basis evidence/verification to the supplied local set (with a closed, trusted verifier contract), or explicitly reduce the result to a non-ADR syntactic parser and remove the verified/predecessor-refusal claims; that scope change needs approval before RED.

findings.invariant: The embedded six-action DAG must locally reject malformed predecessor, edge, and input bindings even when external digest targets remain unresolved.
findings.evidence: v4 sorts lists but never requires predecessor_action_ids to equal the distinct predecessor_action_id values in predecessor_output_refs, requires neither to name a different in-scope action at an earlier topological position, and does not bind predecessor-output InputContract.source_ref to either list. action_dag_sha256 and edge_set_sha256 are explicitly unresolved. Profile/direct-link rows only compare the selected subject and outer digests.
adr_citations: ADR-0125 decision-log.md:8539-8565 requires the closed action DAG, exact predecessor-output refs, root/nonroot rules, and EdgeSetEntry; it states no graph, edge, port, parameter, candidate, or contract is inferred.
ADR-0125 decision-log.md:8738-8745 requires Stage validation to reject DAG skip, reorder, branch graft, and cross-output bindings.
findings.worked_counterexample: Set A2's sorted predecessor_action_ids and predecessor_output_refs to A2 itself, give it a predecessor-output InputContract whose source_ref names an unrelated value, and keep its direct subject/digest links self-consistent. It is nonroot and satisfies every stated local sort/root/profile/direct-link rule, despite a self-cycle and unbound input.
findings.consequence: The finite local grammar still permits graph and predecessor substitutions that need no resolver to detect. P3V4-05, P3V4-06, P3V4-08, and P3V4-10 overstate their coverage.
findings.required_correction: Add locally decidable cross-field rules for action membership, strict predecessor order, ID/ref set equality, and predecessor-output contract binding; explicitly test each mutation. Keep genuinely external digest targets unresolved only after these embedded facts are closed.

findings.invariant: Every trusted injection must have a frozen, independently testable interface and no caller-selected schema or hidden policy.
findings.evidence: v4 names HistoricalStudyRevocations and a method call but defines no ABC, input/output types, construction authority, or exact snapshot semantics in its code-pinned tables. Repository search finds no such interface; the only frozen analogous interfaces are ReleaseKeyring and TrustedClock ABCs in trust.py:198-233. Thus a future implementation must invent a trust boundary outside the matrix, while the matrix's tests merely say injection substitution refuses.
adr_citations: ADR-0125 decision-log.md:8359-8362 requires trusted time and revocation snapshot verification for each envelope; the packet plan at 01-capture-admission.md:38-41 requires trusted signer/clock/revocation inputs and a proportional contract matrix.
findings.worked_counterexample: Two implementations can both expose is_unrevoked(snapshot,key_id,key_version,now_ms) but one treats an unknown snapshot as False and the other lazily treats it as an empty unrevoked set; neither behavior is selected by v4, so the same supplied envelope is not locally decidable from the frozen contract.
findings.consequence: P3V4-01/P3V4-04 cannot prove the claimed fail-closed revocation boundary, and a materially trusted seam remains caller/implementation-chosen.
findings.required_correction: Freeze a closed ABC/protocol and its fail-closed semantics in the matrix and module design, including exact-bool handling, unknown snapshots, exceptions, and injected-instance admission. Pin it alongside the schema tables before RED.

summary.reason: Five independent Major defects leave v4 unable to define and prove its stated local envelope set, exact grammar, PCE comparison, issuance chain, embedded DAG, and revocation seam.

preserved_open: no trust.py route or lifecycle effect
required_next_gate: Revise the Phase 0 contract to resolve every Major, then obtain a fresh independent skeptic review before any RED work.
